Your phone can encode H.264. This is what screen mirroring needs.
No H.264 encoder found. Mirroring the screen and converting videos won’t work on this phone.
Your phone can encode HEVC: a sharper picture at the same bitrate on TVs that support it.
No HEVC encoder. That is fine: CastApp uses H.264 instead.
Your phone can encode AAC sound.
No AAC encoder found. Sound for mirroring and converted videos may be missing.
The phone offers screen capture, so mirroring is possible.
This device has no screen capture. Mirroring won’t work, but playing files and channels still does.
Android can hand the sound of apps to CastApp (audio mode and mirroring with sound).
Before Android 10 the phone’s sound can’t be captured. Mirroring works without sound; playing files is fine.
Notifications are allowed, so you can stop a cast from the notification.
Notifications are off. Casting may be stopped by Android, and you can’t stop it from the notification. Allow them in the phone’s app settings.
CastApp is excluded from battery optimization, so casting keeps running with the screen off.
Android may stop CastApp when the screen is off. Open Settings → Battery optimization and allow it.
This phone has an infrared emitter, so it can work as a remote for TVs and receivers with an IR sensor.
No infrared emitter. Only the infrared remote is affected; the network and Bluetooth remotes still work.
The phone can act as a Bluetooth keyboard, for TVs and boxes that take remote keys over Bluetooth.
No Bluetooth on this device. The Bluetooth remote is not available.
This phone’s Bluetooth doesn’t offer the keyboard (HID device) profile. The Bluetooth remote won’t work; use the network or infrared remote.
Couldn’t check: Bluetooth permission is missing, or Bluetooth is switched off. Open the TV remote once and allow Bluetooth, then test again.
You are on the local network. The phone and the TV must be on the same one.
A VPN is active. It can hide the TV from the phone. Switch it off while casting, or allow local network access in the VPN app.
Only mobile data is connected. Connect to the same Wi-Fi as the TV.
No network. Connect to the Wi-Fi of your TV.
The phone allows multicast, which is how CastApp finds TVs and speakers.
Multicast couldn’t be switched on. Finding devices may not work; you can still add them by address.
The port the receiver needs is free.
The receiver of CastApp is running and uses this port itself.
Another app uses the receiver port. Receiving still works on another port, but other phones may take longer to find this one.
Speech models for subtitles are installed.
No speech model installed. Subtitles written by the phone need one: Settings → Subtitles.
